IOHN.|259 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>directed by the Holy Ghost, we know this to be no Sacrament nor necessarie ceremonie, and the other to be. And why do they beleeue the Church in this, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Church defineth which are Sacraments and which not &c.}}and do not credit her affirming the chalice not to be necessarie for the communicants?

''34. A new commaundement.'') The commaundement of mutual loue was giuen before, but manifoldly misconstrued, and abridged by the Iewes to freends onely, to this life onely, for earthly respects onely: but Christ reneweth it and enlargeth it after the forme of his owne loue toward vs, and giueth grace to fulfil it.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''They being sad, because he said that he must goe from them, he comforteth them many waies, as, putting them in hope to folovv him vnto the same place, so that they keepe his commaundements. Where he telleth them, that him self is the vvay thither according to his Humanitie, and also the end according to his Diuinitie, no lesse then his Father, because he is consubstantial. 15 promising also to send vnto them (that is, to his Church) the Holy Ghost to be after his departure with them for euer. 28 And saying that it is his promotion (according to his Humanitie) to goe to the Father, for, whose obedience this his death shalbe, & not for any guilt of his owne.''}} {{dropinitial|L|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial L, a dragon.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=14|verse=1}}}}ET {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō SS. Philip and Iacobs day ''Maij. 1''.}}not your hart be troubled. You beleeue in God, beleeue in me also. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=2}}† In my fathers house there be {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ These mansions signifie differences of glorie in heauen. ''Hiero. li. 2. adu. Iouin''.}}∷ many mansions. If not, I vvould haue told you, Because I goe to prepare you a place. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=3}}† And if I goe, and prepare you a place: I come againe and vvil take you to my self, that vvhere I am, you also may be. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=4}}† And vvhither I goe you knovv, and the vvay you knovv.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=5}}† Thomas saith to him, Lord, vve knovv not vvhither thou goest: and hovv can vve knovv the vvay? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=6}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, I am the vvay, and the veritie, and the life. no man commeth to the Father, but by me. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=7}}† If you had knovven me, my father also certes you had knovven: and from hence forth you {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`doe knovv''}}`shal know' him, and you haue seen him.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=8}}† Philippe saith to him, Lord shevv vs the Father, and it sufficeth vs. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=9}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, So long time I am vvith you: & haue you not knowen me? Philippe, he that seeth me, seeth the Father also. Hovv saiest thou, Shevv vs the father? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=10}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''do ye not believe.''}}∷ Doest thou not beleeue that I am in the Father, & the Father in me? The vvordes that I speake to you, of my self I speake not. But my father that abideth in me, he doeth the vvorkes. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=11}}† Beleeue you not, that I am in the Father and the Father in me? Otherwise for the vvorkes them selues beleeue. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=12}}† Amen, amen I say to you, he that beleeueth in me, the vvorkes that I doe, he also shal doe, and {{sup|‖}} greater then these shal he doe, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=13}}† because I goe to the Father, and vvhatsoeuer you shal aske in my<noinclude>{{rh||Kk ij|name,}}</noinclude>
